content: The rates of DNA testing and the initiation of treatment among eligible individuals remain a critical area of focus. Further research is required to evaluate the impact of point-of-care (POC) HBV DNA testing compared to non-POC testing on the hepatitis B virus (HBV) care cascade. The study by Seto WK et al. (2018) in The Lancet highlights the global burden of chronic HBV infection and the need for improved diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Similarly, Jeng WJ et al. (2023) in The Lancet emphasize the importance of advancing HBV management to reduce disease progression and complications. Hsu YC et al. (2023) in Nature Reviews Gastroenterology & Hepatology call for action to address missed opportunities in HBV care, particularly in resource-limited settings. The World Health Organization (WHO) has also provided guidelines on HBV and HCV testing, emphasizing the need for accessible and effective diagnostic tools. Fanning GC et al. (2019) in Nature Reviews Drug Discovery discuss therapeutic strategies aimed at achieving a functional cure for HBV, while Huang DQ et al. (2023) in Hepatology demonstrate the significant reduction in hepatocellular carcinoma risk with antiviral therapy in chronic HBV patients. The American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) 2018 guidelines, as outlined by Terrault NA et al. (2018) in Hepatology, provide updated recommendations on the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of chronic HBV. Similarly, Nguyen MH et al. (2020) in Clinical Microbiology Reviews review advances in HBV prevention, diagnosis, and therapy. The Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver (APASL) guidelines, as detailed by Kumar M et al. (2022) in Hepatology International, address HBV management during pregnancy, highlighting the importance of maternal and neonatal care. Conners EE et al. (2023) in MMWR Recommendations and Reports provide CDC recommendations for HBV screening and testing in the United States, emphasizing the need for early detection and linkage to care. López-Martínez R et al. (2019) in Journal of Clinical Microbiology demonstrate the effectiveness of a one-step strategy for hepatitis C virus (HCV) diagnosis in central laboratories, which could serve as a model for HBV elimination efforts. Bartlett SR et al. (2019) in Liver International evaluate the population-level care cascade for HCV in British Columbia, Canada, highlighting the impact of direct-acting antivirals on treatment outcomes. The National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) (2012) provides public health guidance on promoting HBV and HCV testing among high-risk populations, while the Royal College of Pathologists (2015) offers recommendations on the retention and storage of pathological records and specimens. Trickey A et al. (2023) in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology compare the impact of POC HCV RNA viral load testing with laboratory-based testing, demonstrating improved uptake of RNA testing and treatment with reduced turnaround times. Tang W et al. (2022) in Diagnostics (Basel) assess the diagnostic accuracy of POC HCV viral load assays, emphasizing their potential to enhance HCV diagnosis and care. Kachimanga C et al. (2020) in Heliyon report on HBV screening and linkage to care among medical students in Sierra Leone, while Kawana W et al. (2022) describe the integration of HBV into HIV programs in sub-Saharan Africa. Nyama ET et al. (2023) in Journal of Viral Hepatitis highlight the challenges of HBV treatment in rural sub-Saharan Africa, focusing on treatment initiation and outcomes in Sierra Leone. Picchio CA et al. (2023) in Communications Medicine demonstrate the effectiveness of community-based HBV screening in enhancing linkage to care among West African migrants in Spain. Shih G et al. (2020) in Journal of Viral Hepatitis present a same-day test and treat model for chronic HCV and HBV infection, showing promising results from community-based pilot studies in Egypt. Ndow G et al. (2023) provide additional data on the turnaround time from HBsAg testing to HBV DNA viral load assessment using GeneXpert for both plasma and dried blood spot samples. Johannessen A et al. (2023) evaluate the time between key steps in the HBV care cascade for POC DNA testing in Ethiopia, while Nyama ET et al. (2023) report similar findings in Sierra Leone. Picchio CA et al. (2023) and Shih G et al. (2020) provide insights into the effectiveness of POC testing in Spain and Egypt, respectively. The systematic review and meta-analysis by Tao Y et al. (2024) assess the diagnostic performance of POC HBV viral load assays compared to laboratory-based nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs), highlighting their potential to decentralize testing and improve access in resource-limited settings.
